verdict_rationale: The metric is a correct, deterministic mir_eval-style onset F1 with a tight, faithful self-check, and models separate well; but the held-out audio is four public General MIDI soundfonts through FluidSynth, which the prompt does not say. The score therefore rewards fingerprinting the renderer from the 10 public clips (which every wallet winner did). The 0.553 floor (untouched YourMT3+) also zeros 33 of 57 trials.
floor: 0 = 0.553 macro onset F1 of the untouched YourMT3+ checkpoint on the 271 held-out clips (task.yaml:58-64), measured by direct batched inference at 365.81x real time, not through HTTP serving or the byte cap. It is a strong off-the-shelf baseline, far above trivial (an empty or constant prediction scores 0 raw). Sensible as 'beat the public SOTA checkpoint', but it is undisclosed and it zeros every from-scratch model below 0.553 (33 of 57 trials, 5 of the 18 audited). The prompt does not hint that untouched YourMT3+ scores 0.27 on the public clips but 0.55 on the held-out ones.
ceiling: 1 = exact-reference oracle (task.yaml:63). Not binding (best 0.908 raw = 79.5 Sonnet $50; 76.7 Astra $200). It is reachable in principle on synthetic renders, which is part of why soundfont matching pays off.
usable_range: observed 0-79.5 of 0-100 across 57 trials (nonzero 9/5/10 of 19 at $10/$50/$200); range above the floor is well used by the top agents.
feasible_at_10: yes: Sonnet 73.8 and Opus 61.9 at $10. Rendering MIDI through free soundfonts is CPU-cheap, and a YourMT3+ fine-tune or a compact CNN fits in about 2.9 H100 hours.
budget_scaling: Mixed: Astra 49.4 -> 73.4 -> 76.7 scales; Opus 61.9 / 61.0 / 64.3 is flat; Fable 28.8 / 47.2 / 28.1 tracks whether it matched soundfonts, not money. All-model means 15.4 / 15.6 / 20.9. Method choice (timbre matching) matters more than compute.
selfcheck_fidelity: High for the gates: the size gate, then a 271-request pass (public clips cycled ~27x under new IDs) at concurrency 16 against grading's 162.6 s formula, with up to 2x patience so a too-slow server still gets a measured factor, then one clip through the parser (verifier.py:141-206). Gaps: no review; no held-out-like score, because the 10 public clips are much harder for pretrained models than the held-out set (untouched YourMT3+ about 0.27 public vs 0.553 held-out), so agents cannot tell whether they clear the floor; repeated clips flatter a caching server (noted to the agent, verifier.py:185-188); and the run time of autoregressive decoders scales with note density, which may differ between the public and held-out clips (suspected).
judge: none for the metric (amt_notes.py, deterministic). The review is Claude Opus 5.5 (global).
neutrality: No judge and no harness-specific data. Favours agents that know of YourMT3+/MT3 (it defines the floor) or, more strongly, that think of fingerprinting the synthetic renderer: all three Opus runs, all three Astra runs and Fable 3zcox2 did this. The soundfont list appears only in the trusted review policy, never in the agent's materials, so the advantage is in discovering it, open to any harness.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared smoke fixture: /transcribe returns no notes (solution/server.py:134, 'no notes, F1 0 (the zero floor)'), which scores 0 raw and fails the review. The operator's YourMT3+ baseline (pipeline/amt_yourmt3.py) is the floor. Trials show the task can be solved well past it (0.908 raw).

issues.finding: The held-out audio is FluidSynth renders through four public GM soundfonts, and both splits use all four. The contract instead says the held-out clips have 'a range of instrument sounds', and the review policy, which agents never see, names the exact banks as fine to train on. Fingerprinting the renderer from the public clips is therefore allowed and decisive, and the score measures fit to four synthetic timbre sets more than music transcription.

issues.finding: The noise is moderate: 271 clips from 200 catalog selections (one 30 s excerpt per MIDI file), with per-class F1 pooled over clips and then macro-averaged over 9 classes. Sparse classes (such as mallets and pipe) each carry 1/9 of the score on few clips. A clip-bootstrap SE of about 0.011 raw (~2.5 points, plausibly 2-3.5) is estimated, not computed (per-clip counts are not available locally).

issues.finding: The real-time gate is all-or-nothing: the whole 271-clip pass must finish within 162.6 s at concurrency 16, or the score is 0. The self-check reproduces it on the grading hardware, and no audited trial was zeroed by it.

issues.finding: The headline averages over classes present in the reference, while the contract says 'the mean of the nine class F1s'. These are identical if all nine classes occur in the held-out set (likely; not verified). One malformed note (for example offset == onset) fails the whole clip, which then counts toward the 5% run-failure limit.
